target: Original PSP PlayStation Network release via PPSSPP; Ad Hoc reachable, official infrastructure retired

areas.name: Run Setup
areas.location_cue: The PSP package, PPSSPP profile, and first title-screen load.
areas.note: The original PlayStation Network PSP release is the sole content route.

levels.1: Keep the downloadable handheld build as the authority.
levels.2: Use a personally preserved PSP package through PPSSPP.
levels.3: Load the original North American NPUG-80114 package, or a verified equivalent regional release, in a dedicated PPSSPP profile. Do not substitute the smaller preview embedded in Logan's Shadow.

levels.1: Confirm that all editor environments are present.
levels.2: The full game exposes four customizable environments.
levels.3: Open Mission Modifier and verify that Fortress, Village, Aerospace, and Ruins are selectable. If only one environment appears, you launched the Logan's Shadow preview rather than the full release.

levels.1: Protect the preserved package and created missions.
levels.2: Back up the PSP savedata and user-mission files.
levels.3: Confirm the profile reloads normally, then copy its PPSSPP savedata and mission files before emulator upgrades. Use save states only for testing; saved missions should survive a full application restart.

levels.1: Map the handheld camera controls comfortably.
levels.2: Bind movement, face-button camera input, aiming, and modifier shortcuts.
levels.3: Create a game-specific controller profile. A right-stick remap for PSP camera buttons is safe, but do not enable cheats that alter rank, inventory, movement, object limits, or match scoring.

levels.1: Treat this as a multiplayer construction game.
levels.2: There is no story route, collectible campaign, or ending.
levels.3: Completion consists of the built-in mission library, editor environments and tools, playable Ad Hoc rules, armory and avatar records, plus an honest archive of retired infrastructure features.

areas.name: Availability and Preservation
areas.location_cue: The opening network choice and PPSSPP multiplayer configuration.
areas.note: Official infrastructure is retired; local Ad Hoc is the reachable play branch.

levels.1: Separate local play from the closed hosted service.
levels.2: Infrastructure features stopped operating on 27 June 2012.
levels.3: Do not wait for an official login to succeed. Hosted matchmaking, ranked progression, shared-mission browsing, ratings, friends, cells, and community lists are historical records unless a verified preservation service adds Combat Ops support.

levels.1: Recheck community support before each serious run.
levels.2: Combat Ops is absent from the preservation-service list checked on 28 July 2026.
levels.3: Consult the current preservation-service compatibility page before configuring infrastructure. If Combat Ops is still absent, keep every infrastructure-only record marked unavailable rather than borrowing settings from Dark Mirror or Logan's Shadow.

levels.1: Use the local wireless branch with real partners.
levels.2: Connect two or more matching PPSSPP clients through Ad Hoc networking.
levels.3: Use legally preserved matching regional builds, align PPSSPP networking settings, enter the same private Ad Hoc room, and complete a short test match. Up to eight participants are supported.

levels.1: Editor access does not create computer opponents.
levels.2: Use at least one real second participant to complete combat tests.
levels.3: Build and save missions alone if needed, but use another player for match completion. Do not claim that walking an empty editor map replaces the multiplayer portion.

levels.1: Finish everything the surviving local branch exposes.
levels.2: Complete editor, built-in, armory, and Ad Hoc checks; archive retired records separately.
levels.3: A present-day clean record includes every locally accessible menu, environment, mode, official mission, object tool, avatar, and armory entry. Infrastructure XP, downloads, uploads, ratings, and locked skins remain unavailable unless service preservation becomes real.

areas.note: The full release contains four construction settings with multiple zone combinations.

levels.1: Open each distinct construction setting.
levels.2: Select Fortress from Mission Modifier's environment list.
levels.3: Create a new mission, choose Fortress, confirm a Central Zone, and inspect every offered Alpha and Beta attachment without assuming that another environment's pieces are identical.

levels.1: Open each distinct construction setting.
levels.2: Select Village from Mission Modifier's environment list.
levels.3: Create a new mission, choose Village, confirm a Central Zone, and inspect every offered Alpha and Beta attachment without assuming that another environment's pieces are identical.

levels.3: Create a new mission, choose Ruins, confirm a Central Zone, and inspect every offered Alpha and Beta attachment without assuming that another environment's pieces are identical.

areas.name: Combat Types
areas.location_cue: The Combat Type menu reached during the second editor phase.
areas.note: Each rule set has different validity requirements.

levels.1: Build and finish a match using this rule set.
levels.2: Select Deathmatch in Combat Type and make the mission valid.
levels.3: Configure Deathmatch: Every participant scores independently. Place every required spawn or objective marker, save only after the validity check passes, then finish one Ad Hoc match with a real partner.

levels.1: Build and finish a match using this rule set.
levels.2: Select Team Deathmatch in Combat Type and make the mission valid.
levels.3: Configure Team Deathmatch: Two forces compete through combined eliminations. Place every required spawn or objective marker, save only after the validity check passes, then finish one Ad Hoc match with a real partner.

levels.1: Build and finish a match using this rule set.
levels.2: Select Retrieval in Combat Type and make the mission valid.
levels.3: Configure Retrieval: Teams move an objective beacon to a scoring point. Place every required spawn or objective marker, save only after the validity check passes, then finish one Ad Hoc match with a real partner.

levels.1: Build and finish a match using this rule set.
levels.2: Select Sabotage in Combat Type and make the mission valid.
levels.3: Configure Sabotage: Teams obtain a code and attack the opposing warhead. Place every required spawn or objective marker, save only after the validity check passes, then finish one Ad Hoc match with a real partner.

levels.1: Build and finish a match using this rule set.
levels.2: Select Rogue Agent in Combat Type and make the mission valid.
levels.3: Configure Rogue Agent: A neutral credential transfers the empowered role between players. Place every required spawn or objective marker, save only after the validity check passes, then finish one Ad Hoc match with a real partner.

areas.name: Built-In Mission Library
areas.location_cue: The official mission list available before opening community downloads.
areas.note: Twenty developer-made missions shipped with the full release.

levels.1: Work through the entire official list.
levels.2: Complete every one of the twenty shipping missions.
levels.3: Filter the mission browser to official content, begin at the first entry, and remain through each match result until all twenty have a recorded play. Individual historical menu names were not safely established in the corpus, so this pack does not invent them.

levels.1: Use one shipping mission as a starting point.
levels.2: Load an official mission and change at least one valid combat element.
levels.3: Choose an official mission, enter its modifier, alter a spawn, objective, combat object, or navigation object, give the copy a new name, pass validation, save it, and complete a local test.

levels.1: Check that saved work survives a restart.
levels.2: Reload every locally created or remixed mission from Memory Stick storage.
levels.3: Close the game fully, relaunch it, open Load User Mission, and confirm each completed editor exercise remains listed and can enter its review screen.

areas.name: Mission Modifier
areas.location_cue: The first editor phase, before entering the map as a combatant.
areas.note: This phase assembles terrain, lighting, weather, and factions.

levels.1: Start with an empty local design rather than a downloaded map.
levels.2: Choose Create New Mission and advance to Area of Operations.
levels.3: Begin a fresh mission, select one of the four environments, and proceed only after each required menu displays a checkmark.

levels.1: Choose the required core of the map.
levels.2: Assign one Central Zone layout.
levels.3: Review every Central Zone choice for the selected environment, select one, and confirm it as the mission's mandatory core.

levels.1: Extend one side of the core.
levels.2: Attach an available Alpha Zone.
levels.3: Open the Alpha attachment list, inspect its available terrain pieces, connect one compatible option, and verify the overview map updates.

levels.1: Extend the remaining side.
levels.2: Attach an available Beta Zone.
levels.3: Choose a compatible Beta attachment, then inspect the complete Central, Alpha, Beta footprint on the overview map.

levels.1: Try both lighting states.
levels.2: Save one daytime and one nighttime variant.
levels.3: In Mission Logistics, switch the same layout between day and night, save distinct local copies, and load each once to verify the setting.

levels.1: Exercise the environmental controls.
levels.2: Test clear, fog, rain, snow, dust, and flooding wherever offered.
levels.3: Cycle through every weather choice the selected environment exposes. Save and load at least one altered-weather version; do not claim an option on maps where the menu omits it.

levels.1: Assign both sides deliberately.
levels.2: Choose a valid avatar faction for each force.
levels.3: Open Mission Combatants, set Force A and Force B to distinct available factions, then verify the review screen records both selections.

levels.1: Inspect the full assembled footprint.
levels.2: Open the overview during both editor phases.
levels.3: Use the overview shortcut before placing objects and again after the mission validates. Confirm zone links, spawn coverage, and objective separation.

areas.name: Combat Modifier
areas.location_cue: The second editor phase, entered as a third-person combatant inside the assembled map.
areas.note: This phase places objectives, spawns, combat objects, and navigation tools.

levels.1: Learn where the editor permits objects.
levels.2: Approach and activate the red wireframe positions.
levels.3: Walk the map in Combat Modifier, aim at each red wireframe box, and open its assignment menu. Objects can only occupy supported boxes.

levels.1: Give the first team a valid entry.
levels.2: Assign at least one spawn location to Force A.
levels.3: Select an allowed spawn box, activate it, assign Force A, and confirm the validity panel counts it.

levels.1: Give the second team a valid entry.
levels.2: Assign at least one spawn location to Force B.
levels.3: Activate a separate supported spawn box for Force B and verify that both teams now satisfy the mode's minimum.

levels.1: Objective modes require their own markers.
levels.2: Place the required markers for Retrieval, Sabotage, and Rogue Agent.
levels.3: Switch through the three objective modes, activate their required objective boxes, assign Force A, Force B, or Neutral as appropriate, and rename the markers only if the mission remains valid.

levels.1: Add an environmental combat object.
levels.2: Activate a supported barrel position.
levels.3: Open Combat Objects at a wireframe box, choose a barrel option, stay within the displayed object limit, and verify it appears in the review.

levels.1: Use a supported defensive position.
levels.2: Activate a turret at a valid box.
levels.3: Find a turret-compatible box, place the turret, confirm its facing in a local test, and move or remove it if it controls a spawn unfairly.

levels.1: Populate the map's loadout choices.
levels.2: Place and configure a weapon crate.
levels.3: Activate a weapon box, choose an available armory entry, and test that the crate supplies the selected item during a local match.

levels.1: Add one rapid traversal object.
levels.2: Activate an RTL-compatible navigation box.
levels.3: Choose RTL under Navigation Objects, place it only at a supported connection, and test both its entry and landing during an Ad Hoc match.

levels.1: Use height to create a one-way route.
levels.2: Place a zipline between compatible elevations.
levels.3: Find a zipline-supported box with sufficient height difference, activate it, and complete a test ride without landing outside the playable terrain.

levels.1: Open a supported vertical path.
levels.2: Place a ladder in a navigation box.
levels.3: Activate a ladder-compatible box, confirm both ends connect to walkable surfaces, and climb it in a test match.

levels.1: Use a supported obstacle or step.
levels.2: Activate a crate navigation object.
levels.3: Place a crate at a permitted box, then test that it does not block a required spawn or objective route.

levels.1: Use the editor's navigation shortcut.
levels.2: Jump between provided vantage positions.
levels.3: During Combat Modifier, use the vantage shortcut at least once in each zone and inspect hard-to-reach object boxes without treating the shortcut as a player route.

levels.1: Move quickly between editing zones.
levels.2: Use teleport to reach another map section.
levels.3: Open the editor navigation controls, teleport to a different zone, and confirm the location panel updates to the correct map section.

levels.1: Name and describe the local design.
levels.2: Set a location name and a concise objective description.
levels.3: Use Mission Text Editor to enter an original title and plain mechanical description. Avoid story claims or copied community text.

levels.1: Do not save an invalid design.
levels.2: Reach a valid review state.
levels.3: Open Mission Review, check terrain, logistics, combatants, mode, spawns, objectives, and object limits, then correct every invalid marker before saving.

levels.1: Prove the mission file is durable.
levels.2: Name, save, close, and reload the mission.
levels.3: Save the valid mission to Memory Stick storage, exit to the main menu, load it again, and verify the review settings match the original design.
